era_setting.place: Port Valdez and Prince William Sound, Alaska; the marine terminal and its berths; a United States courtroom
era_setting.notes: The grounding is 24 March 1989. The film reaches back to a 1985 treatment record and forward to the Supreme Court on 25 June 2008. A 1989 tanker and terminal: analogue bridge instruments, paper charts, no flat panels, 1989 clothing and vehicles. The courtroom scenes are 2000s. Nothing from the 2010s or 2020s may appear as present day. This is coastal Alaska -- spruce, snow, grey water, mountains to the sea.

forbidden_claims: Any probable cause for the grounding. It is stated in NTSB/MAR-90/04, which is a 257-page pure scan with no text layer and has NOT been read on this machine (FACTS_LEDGER trap note). Until it is read, this film states no probable cause at all. This is the single most important line in this list.

That the master was drunk at the wheel, was steering, or caused the grounding. The vessel was under the navigational control of the third mate (FACTS_LEDGER row VZ-003). What the record supports about the master is a 1985 treatment and an employer that did not follow it up (VZ-301 to VZ-308).

That the third mate was negligent, or was asleep. The Board concludes he could have had as little as 5 or 6 hours of sleep in the previous 24 and was working beyond his normal watch period (VZ-106, VZ-107), and that fatigue COULD have overcome him (VZ-109). It does not find that it did.

That Exxon was uniquely bad among tanker operators. The Board records that the chief-mate practice producing a 6-on-6-off watch is widely practised (VZ-201), and it addressed all six recommendations to every shipping company operating in Prince William Sound.
Any figure for oil spilled other than about 258,000 barrels. Gallon figures in circulation vary; convert only against a cited source (VZ-005).

That the Supreme Court let Exxon off. The Court applied a ratio rule to a compensatory figure. Exxon had already spent $2.1 billion on cleanup and paid at least $1.2 billion more in settlements and voluntary payments (VZ-501 to VZ-504).
Anything about oiled wildlife, dead animals or shoreline carcasses. Out of scope of both sources, and it is the imagery that has always buried the manning finding.
That the accident happened because one man left the bridge. The Supreme Court's summary says that; the safety record's findings are about manning, scheduling and appraisal (VZ-201 to VZ-216).
That any recommendation was adopted, implemented or closed. Whether the six were ever classified as closed is an open item in the ledger and is not sourced.
Anything about the Oil Pollution Act of 1990, double hulls or escort tugs as an outcome of this accident. Source S5 has not been opened.

That the master was removed from employment, or what happened to him afterwards. The Board says Exxon SHOULD have removed him until there was proof the problem was controlled (VZ-308). That is a recommendation, not a record of what occurred.
That fatigue caused the grounding. The Board's letter is about the conditions that produce a fatigued crew. Causation belongs to the report that has not been read.

beats.headline: ICE ON ONE SIDE, REEF ON THE OTHER
RATED ON WILLINGNESS TO WORK OVERTIME

notes: EP82 of the EP77-82 slate. Runtime and word bands follow the owner's 2026-08-23 decision: 29-32 minutes, divided at the measured 160 wpm, never 176. Two primary sources read in full: NTSB Safety Recommendation M-90-26/-31 and Exxon Shipping Co. v. Baker, 554 U.S. 471 from the official United States Reports. The main NTSB report MAR-90/04 is a pure scan with no text layer and has NOT been read here, which is why forbidden_claims begins by banning any statement of probable cause. The controlling idea, never spoken: a manning level is a promise about how tired somebody will be. Motif: a bunk in a ship's cabin -- made and empty, turned back, slept in for two hours, made again. forbidden_subjects bans the grounding itself, the wreck, and every image of oiled wildlife: that imagery is the reason nobody remembers the manning table, and the manning table is the film. It also bans hull lettering and funnel markings, because EP79 produced a real airline's logo with the ban already in the NEG line and EP80 produced a real cruise line's funnel colour -- the order must say plain and unmarked in the SUBJECT, not only in the negatives.
